dropped.finding: The newly-added botocore read-timeout classification arm in failure._map (WAIT_AND_RETRY for ReadTimeoutError/ConnectTimeoutError from a botocore module) has no test. The new test file drives the disposition-forwarding chain only with a synthetic WAIT_AND_RETRY LLMOutcome manually attached to the exception, never exercising _map/classify_llm_failure with a real botocore-shaped exception, so a regression that removed or broke this arm (reclassifying the outage as NEEDS_INVESTIGATION -> non-retryable -> exit 1) would not be caught.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add a table-driven test constructing a fake exception with type(exc).__name__ == 'ReadTimeoutError' and __module__ == 'botocore.exceptions' (and one for ConnectTimeoutError), pass through classify_llm_failure, and assert outcome.resolution_class is ResolutionClass.WAIT_AND_RETRY and outcome.retryable is True; add a negative case where the same class name from a non-botocore module does NOT get WAIT_AND_RETRY.

Consumer re-checks the flag: src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:631 `_rc = 11 if (_outcome and _outcome.retryable) else 1`
dropped.finding: `_reconstructed_outcome` is named/documented as rebuilding a RETRYABLE disposition, but its guard only checks that the `retryable` key is PRESENT (`"retryable" not in failure_diagnostic`) — it reconstructs any disposition regardless of the flag's value, e.g. a NEEDS_INVESTIGATION with `retryable: False`. Functionally harmless (close_precheck.py:631 re-checks `_outcome.retryable`, so a non-retryable reconstruction still maps to exit 1), but the name/docstring over-promise and could mislead a future maintainer into assuming the returned outcome is always retryable.
